title: There's No Freaking Way I'll be Your Lover! Unless...
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Renako Amaori, a friendless recluse in middle school, reinvents herself to join the popular crowd in high school and soon becomes best friends with Mai Oduka, a teen supermodel. When Mai confesses romantic love, Renako insists friendship is better, and the two agree to a contest over whether they should be best friends or lovers. Other girls in the group also fall for Renako in a comedic yuri harem; manga adaptation of a light novel.
life_message: Being honest about who you are and what you feel, even when it is awkward, is how you find real closeness.

content.note: Social anxiety comedy; Mai mistakenly thinks Renako is about to take her own life on the rooftop (Wikipedia).

Teen yuri romance with ecchi genre label (batch, MU), big-breast and 'aggressive lover' tags; MU lists Sexual Assault and Rape (low votes). A critic of the novel objected to Mai disregarding Renako's lack of consent (Wikipedia, reception). Renako later dates two girls in a consensual non-monogamous relationship (Wikipedia; AniList Polyamorous).
Renako's social anxiety and past as a non-attending recluse; masks worn by Mai and Kaho (Wikipedia).
Pressing romantic advances on a reluctant friend played for comedy (Wikipedia reception; MU Aggressive Lover).
Modeling, fashion, gaming and cosplay fame (Wikipedia).

dominant: Self-reinvention and authenticity; same-sex romance; polyamory as a happy ending

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are fought as playful contests and talks; no honor feuds.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The girls choose their own relationships, ending in a self-defined non-monogamous arrangement.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friend group matters more than family, though Mai's mother and maid exert pressure.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School popularity hierarchy exists but is shown as a mask the girls want to drop.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern, secular setting; love defined by personal choice.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Authenticity, self-reinvention and emotional honesty are the core values.

folkways.japan: School-caste popularity, keeping up appearances (tatemae) and the established yuri genre are Japanese context for the story, described not judged.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia: reviewer notes "very, very panicky" narration and consent concerns; nothing on preachiness (to verify).
delivery.note: Its view of honest love is carried by Renako's narration and choices; the opposing maid's portrayal is unverified.

winners_losers: Renako, Mai and Ajisai win a happy non-monogamous romance; the maid Hanatori, who opposes Renako, loses. Sympathy rests with self-expression and chosen love.
